notes: RAF jet carrying the UK defence secretary: about 30 min of GPS jamming near Kaliningrad on the flight back from Orzysz, Poland, plus a shorter episode that morning. Confirmed by the UK Prime Minister's spokesperson. Exact position and time not public: box and whole day are approximate.

Two Finnair Helsinki-Tartu flights turned back because the GPS-based approach to Tartu was unusable; Finnair suspended the route 29 Apr-31 May 2024. Article of 30 Apr says 'last Thursday': date 25 Apr inferred. Box: Tartu approach area.

Joint Estonia-Latvia-Lithuania letter to the ITU (TTJA ref. 17-5/2025/0199, 19 Feb 2025), Annex 2: Lithuanian spectrum monitoring detected emissions on GNSS bands from the Kaliningrad region on this date; aircraft affected. Jamming or spoofing not stated. Box: Kaliningrad and Lithuania.
Same ITU letter, Annex 2: Lithuanian spectrum monitoring, emissions from the Kaliningrad region on this date.
Stanford GPS Lab (Lo et al., ION ITM 2026): spoofing near Kaliningrad first seen on this date, alongside regular jamming. Found in ADS-B data, so not independent of this project's input.
Same ITU letter, Annex 2: on this date Lithuanian monitoring recorded a wideband emission affecting all GNSS bands (GPS L1/L2/L5, GLONASS, Galileo) from the Kaliningrad region.

Same ITU letter, Annex 1: aircraft reports in Estonian airspace on 7-9 Feb 2025; the Narva monitoring station measured interference at 1575.4, 1561.0 and 1602.0 MHz from bearings 26-27 and 70-72 degrees (Leningrad Region). Box: eastern Estonia and Gulf of Finland, east edge at the study region's 28.5E.

Stanford GPS Lab (Lo et al., ION ITM 2026, Fig. 8): omnidirectional jamming of about 250 km radius around Kaliningrad, from ADS-B NIC values. Not independent of this project's input. Box clipped to the study region.

Stanford GPS Lab (Lo et al., ION ITM 2026, Figs. 4, 9-11): four spoofing events near Kaliningrad (fixed points, semicircle then straight line), including an ERJ-135 (OE-LOW) jammed then spoofed, checked against MLAT and the flight plan. ADS-B based.

Stanford GPS Lab (Lo et al., ION ITM 2026): a ground receiver (u-blox monitor) in Gdynia, Poland recorded jamming on L1 and L5 attributed to Kaliningrad; no spoofing seen. Ground measurement, independent of ADS-B. Box: Gdansk Bay area.

Spanish military jet carrying the defence minister had a GPS disturbance near Kaliningrad early on 24 Sep on the way to Siauliai, Lithuania; confirmed by the Spanish Defence Ministry. Position and time approximate.
Aircraft carrying the European Commission President lost GPS on approach to Plovdiv, Bulgaria; stated by the Bulgarian government. Outside the study regions: listed, not checked.

Severe GPS spoofing over Delhi in the week before 6 Nov 2025, starting about 60 NM from IGI airport while ILS on runway 10/28 was out of service; seven flights diverted to Jaipur on the night of 4 Nov (date inferred from 'Tuesday night'); DGCA collecting reports. Later confirmed by the government in Parliament. Box: about 60 NM around IGI.

Ryanair flight from London could not land at Vilnius on the evening of Thursday 16 Jan 2025 (date inferred from the article of Friday 17 Jan): GPS interference and a ground-proximity warning on approach; it diverted to Warsaw. Confirmed by Oro Navigacija (Lithuanian air navigation). Box: Vilnius approach; period: 16:00-24:00 UTC.

Pakistan CAA paper to the ICAO DGCA conference (Jul-Aug 2025): GNSS RFI events peaked at 165 in February 2025, Lahore FIR among the most affected. No day or place given; adsb.lol has no Punjab data in 2025, so not checkable from this archive. Listed for the record.

Minister of State for Civil Aviation, written reply in the Lok Sabha (Mar 2026): airlines reported 623 GPS spoofing incidents in Delhi airspace (about 60 NM around IGI) in January-February 2026. About 10 a day, so checked on three fixed days: 15 Jan, 1 Feb and 15 Feb 2026.

Heavy GPS jamming around the port of Constanta, Romania, on 4-5 Jun 2026 (GPSJam data of 4 Jun), before a Ukrainian sea drone that lost navigation exploded in the port; Romania's interim defence minister said the jamming was very strong. Box: Constanta and the coast to Mangalia.

ItaMilRadar map from AirNav Radar data, 3 Nov 2026: significant interference over Romania, Bulgaria and the western Black Sea. Aircraft data, so not independent of this project's input. Box: western Black Sea within the study region.
Same ItaMilRadar map, 3 Nov 2026: significant interference near Kaliningrad, Lithuania and eastern Poland. Aircraft data.
